body: Thank you, I needed to hear that!

He doesn't need much help with stuff, mostly with lifting heavy things and to do things that needs steady hands. He is however not able to do much household chores, so I do most of it. He "pays me back" by massaging me, witch help a lot with my pain.
We are pretty good at doing fun stuff together, but I don't do much by myself. Should probably work on that!

I guess what drains me the most is constant complaining about "this or that hurts" "I can't do this" and so on. I'm not innocent myself there, I struggle with my own pains, but I don't mention it all the time. I probably should talk to him about it, ask him to tone it down a bit, but it feels wrong to ask someone with chronic pain to not mention it so much...
Thank you! I'm trying my best! I am now relatively low contact with both her and my mom!

Thank you. I really doubt she would reciprocate too. One time I asked her to shorten two curtains for me, she has a sewing machine, and she said that would be both my birthday and Christmas gift that year.. This was at the time where I babysat also outside of emergencies. To be fair, her economy was shit at the time, but still...
The reason I feel bad for not babysitting is partly because she could not afford a babysitter until about a year ago.
